nodes.question: What are cultural biases according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Cultural biases are shared fundamental values and beliefs about human and physical nature related to social relations, including values like equality, freedom, order, and good/bad luck.
nodes.paragraph: Each worldview represents a coherent package of pat- terns of social relations and cultural biases. Cultural biases are shared fundamental values (equality, freedom, order, and good/bad luck) and beliefs (underlying problem definitions, positions, strategies, and preferred policy instruments) about human and physical nature related to the four types of social relations (Newman et al., 2018; Oli & Swedlow, 2022; Sotirov & Winkel, 2016). Social relations refer to two dimensions: a preference for low or high external rules on human behavior called grid (thus more or less individual free- dom or constraints) and a preference for low or high group , referring to people S prefer - ence of how to organize their interactions with people (ranging from individual choices to collective decisions). The worldviews with their cultural biases and corresponding social relations and their reciprocal reinforcement are hence conceptualized through a grid-group typology (Thompson et al., 1990; see also Sotirov & Winkel, 2016, Swedlow, 2012). The four worldviews are summarized in Fig. 1. Each quadrant along the two axes of high/low group and grid represents one worldview.
